correctness.rationale: Construct the stationary chain and reset clock as independent two-sided processes. The backward reset age is Exp(r), while the directed cycle is stationary uniform, giving a mixture of three planar Brownian resolvent densities and E|X|²=a²+4D/r. The chain vertex complex eigenvalue is -lambda with lambda=3nu/2-i sqrt(3)nu/2, yielding E[v(Y0)·v(Ys)]=a²exp(-3nu s/2)cos(sqrt(3)nu s/2). Conditioning on the last reset between 0 and t and integrating an independent backward age gives C(t)=(a²+4D/r)e^{-rt}+a²r² Re[(e^{-lambda t}-e^{-rt})/(r²-lambda²)]. For r>3nu/2 the oscillatory complex mode is the slow nonzero term, forcing unbounded negative windows; for r<3nu/2 the e^{-rt} coefficient is algebraically positive; at equality the offset 10a²/13+4D/r competes with amplitude 3a²/sqrt13, giving Dc=3nu a²(3sqrt13-10)/104 and all strict/equality cases. Independent nested numerical age/time quadrature agreed in 108 cases to 9e-16, and critical-envelope algebra was cross-checked, but all-times and all-parameters assertions use the analytic proof.

originality.rationale: Classical Poisson resetting and independent random reset positions yield the Bessel resolvent marginal; this part is covered and not asserted as novel. A persistent, autonomously cycling three-state target changes two-time structure while leaving marginal fixed. The relevant new statement is a sharp sign classification of time covariance for a different coupled protocol, not the stationary resolvent formula.

Stationary one-time position mixture is classical renewal theory and must not be claimed novel.
